scoringMethod: Evidence-based review of the pre-change repository. Each dimension is scored only for capabilities implemented in code and supported by existing tests; production-only behavior and external providers are not treated as verified.

dimensions.name: Seguridad y privacidad
evidence: The assistant endpoint resolves the authenticated Supabase user and active profile on the server.
Commercial queries use the authenticated Supabase client and database RLS rather than a service-role bypass.
Sensitive price, cost, GP, margin, commission and PO requests are rejected before normal tool routing for every role.
The LLM receives a redacted copy of tool data and full tool rows are not returned to the browser.
Redaction is blacklist-oriented and does not reliably remove UUIDs, emails, original filenames, raw_value or arbitrary free-text fields.
The router logs up to 500 characters of the user question and a tool summary, creating a content-retention risk.
Business-record content is not explicitly delimited and treated as untrusted instructions in the system prompt.
risks: raw_value and unrecognized properties may be transmitted to OpenAI.
UUIDs, emails and filenames may be present in the provider context despite prompt instructions not to reveal them.
Questions, MPNs or business text may be retained in process logs.
Prompt injection embedded in imported data has no explicit structural defense.

dimensions.name: Integración con Opportunity Finder
evidence: The assistant can produce an opportunities summary through the legacy aggregate opportunities engine.
The certified Opportunity Finder implementation and its persisted jobs/results exist elsewhere in the repository.
Assistant code does not query opportunity_finder_jobs or opportunity_finder_results.
Assistant responses do not consume pipelineVersion, exactMpnMatch, usableAvailabilityMatch or exactQuantityMatch.
The assistant may aggregate up to 30 historical uploads instead of reading the user's selected two-file comparison.
risks: Assistant counts can disagree with the Opportunity Finder UI, CSV and XLSX.
Full sale, partial sale and exact-quantity concepts can be explained using legacy semantics.
The user may receive historical aggregate results when asking about the latest completed comparison.

dimensions.name: Exactitud de intención
evidence: Server-side deterministic routing prevents the model from freely choosing tools.
The router recognizes sensitive requests, stock needs, opportunities, MPN lookup, uploads, import errors, dashboard and employee summaries.
MPN extraction preserves punctuation, hyphens and leading zeros.
Routing is based on ordered regular expressions rather than a central typed intent catalog.
There is no confidence score, ambiguity handling or clarification path.
Help requests and unsupported formulations can fall through to business-record search.
English and Chinese alias coverage is uneven.
risks: The first matching regular expression wins when requests contain multiple intents.
Minor phrasing variations can invoke generic search instead of the intended deterministic tool.
Opportunity Finder terms can be confused with legacy opportunity terms.

dimensions.name: Multidioma
evidence: The UI contains Spanish, English and simplified Chinese labels and persists the selected language.
Language detection recognizes es, en and zh with basic lexical and character heuristics.
The system prompt asks the provider to answer in the selected language.
The widget normally sends the UI language, so automatic detection is often bypassed.
Most deterministic summaries, permission denials and safe fallbacks are hardcoded in Spanish.
Chinese intent recognition is limited and can fall through to generic search.
risks: English and Chinese users can receive Spanish deterministic responses.
Equivalent questions in the three languages may select different tools.
Localized timeout, rate-limit and voice errors are incomplete.

dimensions.name: Robustez de API
evidence: The text and voice endpoints authenticate requests and apply per-user rate limiting.
Missing messages are rejected and inactive or unauthorized profiles return access errors.
Provider failures retain a deterministic text fallback when one exists.
The text endpoint does not enforce a 2000-character maximum or a strict request schema.
Language values fall back to Spanish rather than being rejected when invalid.
Unhandled assistant failures can be converted into HTTP 200 safe fallback responses.
No explicit OpenAI, ElevenLabs or general tool request timeout is configured.
risks: Oversized requests can consume excessive tokens, memory or log capacity.
Clients cannot reliably distinguish an internal failure from a successful answer.
Slow external providers can leave requests open without bounded cancellation.

dimensions.name: Memoria, streaming y experiencia
evidence: A responsive floating widget provides message rendering, loading state, reset and voice controls.
Messages exist only in local React state and are lost on refresh.
Only the current question is sent to the server; the model receives no prior conversation context.
There is no persistent AI conversation schema, history view or conversation deletion.
Responses are returned as complete JSON with no token streaming or progress-event protocol.
There is no request cancellation, copy action, evidence list or generated-versus-deterministic indicator.
Accessibility is partial: buttons have labels, but the panel lacks dialog semantics, focus trapping and a live region.
existingTests: No dedicated React Testing Library coverage for AIAssistantWidget was found in the pre-change baseline.
risks: Users can assume the assistant remembers context that the model never receives.
Long requests cannot be cancelled and may continue after the widget closes.
Keyboard and screen-reader users receive incomplete interaction support.

dimensions.name: Voz
evidence: The implemented flow records audio, transcribes with OpenAI, calls the shared assistant core and synthesizes speech with ElevenLabs.
Audio type and a configurable size limit are validated, and a TTS failure preserves the text response.
No application database write of recorded audio was found.
Audio size is checked after formData parsing rather than before buffering.
The flow lacks explicit consent text, cancellation and provider timeouts.
Successful voice responses can expose an internal traceId.
Physical Safari, iPad and iPhone behavior is not verified.
risks: Large multipart bodies may be buffered before validation.
UUIDs, emails or unnecessary text may be sent to TTS.
Provider retention and real-device behavior remain unverified.

dimensions.name: Rendimiento
evidence: Tool results and examples are limited before being returned to the UI or serialized for the LLM.
The LLM data serialization has an approximate 14000-character cap.
Simple database tools use explicit result limits.
Stock-needs can query up to 20 uploads with 5000 records per upload.
Legacy opportunities can query up to 30 uploads with 5000 records per upload.
Both aggregate paths select raw_data and normalized_data and perform per-upload queries.
There is no assistant result cache, aggregate read model or explicit P95 performance test.
risks: A single question can load 100000 to 150000 rows into application memory.
Per-upload queries create an N+1 pattern and database connection pressure.
Real production latency and memory use are not measured.

dimensions.name: Observabilidad
evidence: The assistant records structured stage, role, scope, tool and timing information.
Persistent rate limiting and sanitized logger infrastructure exist.
Successful info events are printed to stdout but are not inserted into system_logs.
Assistant failures logged as warn can be omitted by dashboards that count only error/fatal.
Questions and tool summaries can be included in logs.
Token usage, fallback use and complete latency metrics are not persisted.
A retention cleanup function exists, but no scheduling mechanism was found in the repository.
risks: Metrics can undercount successful requests and failures.
Logs may retain business content.
Retention of platform stdout and remote production configuration is unverifiable.

dimensions.name: Pruebas y QA
evidence: The pre-change repository has unit coverage for assistant routing, commercial redaction, permission scope, language detection, response normalization, database timeouts, stock needs, legacy opportunities and voice helpers.
The full audited pre-change suite previously completed with 68 test files and 310 passing tests.
TypeScript no-emit validation and ESLint previously passed on this same baseline tree.
Opportunity Finder has independent matcher and API tests, including inventory allocation behavior.
There is no comprehensive HTTP endpoint, React UI, streaming, conversation-memory, adversarial prompt-injection or real-RLS integration suite.
External providers and physical mobile devices are not verified, appropriately leaving this dimension below full score.
risks: Passing unit tests do not demonstrate deployed HTTP status behavior or remote RLS configuration.
There are no UI accessibility, cancellation or mobile-dimension tests.
The assistant is not contract-tested against persisted Opportunity Finder counts or the synthetic Set 01 files.
